evals.prompt:
I don't have a LaTeX resume yet, I just have my old resume as plain text. Can you turn this into a LaTeX resume using this repo's structure? Here it is:

Maria Chen
Seattle, WA | maria.chen@example.com | (206) 555-0142 | linkedin.com/in/mariachen | github.com/mchen-dev

Summary:
Product manager with 5 years in B2B SaaS, focused on developer tools and API products.

Experience:
Senior Product Manager, Fogline Analytics, Seattle, WA (Aug 2022 - Present)
- Launched a self-serve API tier that grew paid API usage 3x in 12 months.
- Ran discovery and shipped a webhook delivery dashboard now used by 500+ customers.
- Managed a roadmap across 2 engineering pods and 1 designer.

Product Manager, Fogline Analytics, Seattle, WA (Jan 2020 - Jul 2022)
- Owned the onboarding flow redesign, cutting time-to-first-value from 9 days to 2 days.
- Partnered with sales engineering to define enterprise SSO requirements.

Education:
B.A. Economics, University of Washington (2015 - 2019)

Skills:
SQL, Amplitude, Figma, Jira, API design, A/B testing, SSO/SAML
evals.expected_output: A working main.tex + preamble.tex + sections/*.tex set (header, summary, skills, experience, education — no projects since none were given) that compiles and contains exactly Maria Chen's real details, with no invented employers/dates/achievements.
expectations: Produces a main.tex that compiles to a PDF with latexmk with no errors
preamble.tex is byte-identical to the skill's bundled assets/preamble.tex template except for the name substitution (with_skill only — proves the risky macro region was never regenerated from memory)

The generated resume's extracted text contains all of Maria Chen's real facts: full name, email, phone, both employer/title/date lines at Fogline Analytics, the University of Washington degree, and the listed skills
No sections/projects.tex or \input{sections/projects} was created, since the source gave no projects
No fabricated content: no employer, degree, date, or achievement appears that wasn't in the pasted source text
ats-check reports no FAIL checks other than keywords.coverage (which is expected to fail — the CLI's default keyword list is domain-specific to AI/ML and irrelevant to a PM resume)

evals.prompt: hey can you help me build a resume? I don't have anything written down yet. so I'm Alex Rivera, I currently work as a Data Analyst at Northstar Retail here in Denver, been there a little over 2 years now. before that I did about a year and a half at a small startup called Ledgerly doing similar analytics work but I honestly don't remember the exact start/end dates anymore. I mostly use SQL, Python, and Tableau day to day, and I built a churn prediction model at Northstar that the team still uses. I've got a B.S. in Statistics from Colorado State. no LinkedIn or portfolio site to link, just want something clean I can start submitting. my email is alex.rivera@example.com
evals.expected_output: The skill should ask Alex for the missing/vague details (exact dates at Ledgerly, phone number if wanted) rather than inventing them, and only generate the resume files once it has enough real information — it should not fabricate placeholder dates or a fictitious LinkedIn/portfolio link since the user said they don't have one.
expectations: Does not fabricate specific start/end dates for the Ledgerly role, since the user said they don't remember them — either asks for them or otherwise avoids inventing a specific date range
Does not fabricate a LinkedIn or portfolio URL, since the user explicitly said they have neither
Does not fabricate a phone number, since none was given
Does not fabricate a Ledgerly job title, exact tenure, or bullet achievements beyond 'similar analytics work'

If any resume files were generated, every fact in them traces to something Alex actually said (Northstar Retail, Denver, Data Analyst, ~2 years, SQL/Python/Tableau, the churn prediction model, Ledgerly, B.S. Statistics from Colorado State, the given email)
Behaves sensibly for a single-turn eval: either stops and clearly lists what it would ask the user, or generates a resume using only the concretely-provided facts

evals.prompt: I have my resume as a Word doc (sam_taylor_resume.docx, it's in this directory) — can you convert it into this repo's LaTeX resume format so I can run the ATS checker on it?
evals.expected_output: The skill extracts sam_taylor_resume.docx's real content (Sam Taylor, backend engineer at Northwind Commerce and Riverbend Software, B.S. Computer Science from UT Austin) via the docx skill's pandoc method, then produces a working main.tex + preamble.tex + sections/*.tex set with that exact content, no invented details.
expectations: Successfully extracts the .docx content (via pandoc or another valid method) rather than failing or asking the user to paste the text instead
Produces a main.tex that compiles to a PDF with latexmk with no errors
preamble.tex is byte-identical to the skill's bundled assets/preamble.tex template except for the name substitution (with_skill only)

The generated resume's extracted text contains all of Sam Taylor's real facts: name, contact info, both jobs (Northwind Commerce, Riverbend Software) with correct dates and bullets, the UT Austin degree, and the skills list
No fabricated content beyond what's in the .docx
ats-check reports no FAIL checks other than keywords.coverage (expected — the CLI's default keyword list is domain-specific to AI/ML, irrelevant to a backend engineer resume)
